correctness.rationale: The exact conditional-cosecant Zak identity reduces the scalar multiplier to an explicit positive rational function of s=sin²(pi x) and y=exp(pi a(1-2 omega)). Its s-derivative has at most one interior maximum because n1=(y+c/y)²+4c sinh²(pi a)>0. The minimum is therefore at s=0 or 1, and monotonicity in y yields all five branches, with equality at every shared endpoint and strict positive lower bound exactly on the stated frame components. Contour integration gives the exact squared norm pi(1+c²)/a, and branch derivatives with reflection c to 1/c give precisely two normalized maxima. The embedded checker passed 14508 supplementary pointwise, endpoint, reciprocity, normalization and Fourier-series checks; the universal proof is analytical.

value.rationale: The quantitative lower bound is the exact reconstruction-stability invariant for a natural two-pole family studied in rational Gabor analysis. Four sharp switching thresholds separate two changes of minimizing Zak fiber from frame collapse, and energy-normalized optimization identifies exactly two optimal pole-residue ratios with a closed form best value. This is a natural design and conditioning problem, not a parameter-renaming or arbitrary finite case.
